chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fadhal, from Ahmad ibn Umar, from Durust al-Wasiti, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah ibn A'yan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
«The marriage of the People of the Book is not permissible.» I said, «May I be your ransom, and where is its prohibition?» He said, «His saying, «And do not hold the ties of the disbelievers»»

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ: People of the Book (Christians and Jews)
key_terms.بِعِمَمِ الْكَافِرَاتِ: Ties of the disbelievers (referring to wives)

ai.seo_question: What is the Quranic evidence for the prohibition of marrying People of the Book in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies that the term 'disbelievers' (al-kafirat) in the verse 'And do not hold the ties of the disbelievers' (3:50) specifically refers to the People of the Book, thereby establishing the prohibition of Muslim men marrying them. This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia scholarly reliance on contextual interpretation (ta'wil) to derive specific legal rulings from general Quranic terms, distinguishing this view from other schools that permit such marriages.
